text:
deploy-bot: Canary health check failed for release r2026.03.15 in eu-west-1. 5xx rate ~12% (threshold 1%). Auto-stop initiated and traffic blocked to canary pool.

olivia: oncall here, looking. seeing a big 503 spike across canary tasks. paging now.

raj: I'm awake, grabbing logs + metrics. are we seeing any quota or autoscale events?

kevin: not seeing autoscale activity. CPU/GPU look normal, but I see repeated backend errors from model-serving pods: 'kv-cache-miss -> OOM' in logs.

maya: who pushed the sticky-cache change? I think sticky-cache eviction flag went live with this rollout.

olivia: correct — feature flag sticky-evict-v2=true rolled in canary 3m before spike.

raj: ok hypothesis: new eviction path causing a burst of cache rebuilds -> memory pressure -> 503s.

incidents-bot: Paging: oncall escalation to @sre-rotation triggered (severity: high). Incident channel created: #incident-2256789123.

olivia: plan: 1) flip feature flag off to stop new evictions 2) drain canary and roll back if needed.

kevin: prepping flag flip. Command via flag service: `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SECRET' https://flags.redwood/api/set -d '{"key":"sticky-evict-v2","value":false,"env":"eu-west-1"}'`

raj: doing it now.

raj: executed flag flip — `sticky-evict-v2=false` returned 200.

maya: metric after flip: 5xx rate down to 6% in last 30s, but still above baseline.

olivia: still customer visible errors — recommend rollback of this canary to previous stable release and redirect traffic.

kevin: ack. rollback command (canary pool):
```
deployctl rollback --region eu-west-1 --pool canary --to-release r2026.03.14 --force
```

raj: initiating rollback now.

deploy-bot: Rollback job started (job id rb-2256789123).

raj: rollback completed on 8/8 canary nodes. health checks green. 5xx now ~0.4% over last 2m.

maya: confirmed - customer-facing error pages reduced to baseline. Looks like rollback fixed immediate issue.

olivia: root cause summary (WIP): sticky cache eviction code path under `sticky-evict-v2` triggers synchronous rebuilds that spike memory allocs under churn, causing OOM and 503s. Canary small sample exposed it.

kevin: logs attached in thread: `logs://rb-2256789123` (link). Key traceback: `kvcache.go:142: panic: runtime: out of memory` followed by container restarts.

raj: action items: 1) revert code in branch, 2) add rate-limited rebuild queue, 3) add circuit breaker on eviction path, 4) add canary mem-safety unit test. I'll file a follow-up PR and link.

olivia: customer impact: spike lasted ~7 minutes during canary traffic only — no global rollout. No large customer report so far, but monitoring someone might have hit errors via QA users.

incidents-bot: Incident severity set to "minor" (internal), auto-created ticket: INC-2256789.

kevin: social note: because auto-stop was enabled we prevented rollout to prod. Good guardrail.

maya: handing off to next oncall (sre-rotation) for monitoring and postmortem. Please include the rb job id and flag change in the doc.

raj: assigning myself to root-cause and fix. I'll publish writeup + timeline.

olivia: thanks team — closing thread here but monitoring for 30m. If anything regresses, ping page. :thumbsup:

sre-rotation: acknowledged handoff. I'll keep an eye on eu-west metrics and update incident ticket if anything weird shows up.

incidents-bot: Thread closed by olivia at 2256789159."
